newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Twenty-one foreigners on crashed Korean jet.
newsitem.headline: Twenty-one foreigners on crashed Korean jet.

text.p: A Korean Air Lines (KAL) jumbo jet that crashed on the Pacific island of Guam on Wednesday was carrying 21 foreigners but most of the passengers were South Korean honeymooners and holidaymakers, Seoul officials said.
The Boeing 747-300 aircraft, with 231 passengers and 23 crew, crashed in a hilly jungle area about three miles (five km) south of Agana International Airport on a scheduled flight from Seoul.
Immigration officials said among passengers aboard Flight 801 were 14 Americans, one Japanese and a New Zealander as well as five unidentified foreign transiting passengers.

Also on the plane were three children and Shin Ki-ha, a four-term lawmaker and former parliamentary leader of the main opposition National Congress for New Politics, his wife and about 20 party members, airline official Kwon Woong-min said.
"Guam is one of most popular Pacific island tourist destinations among Koreans these days. Many honeymooners were on the plane," Kwon said.
KAL Vice President Lee Tae-won said at least 55 people survived the crash.
"So far, 12 people have been admitted to the Guam Memorial Hospital and 15 to the U.S. Naval Hospital," Lee said. "A further 28 people who suffered minor injuries are being pulled out."
Lee's version contradicted other accounts: U.S. Navy officials earlier said 33 survivors had been rescued and there was little chance of finding any others.

Lee said KAL President Cho Yang-ho flew on a special plane to the crash site to head the company's investigation of the incident. He said he suspected failure of a safety device at Guam airport might have caused the crash.
Guam officials have confirmed that the airport's glide slope, a device used for instrument landing during poor visibility, had been out of service for some time.
South Korean President Kim Young-sam called an emergency meeting of cabinet ministers to discuss the crash and ordered all necessary support for the rescue operations.
Kim issued a statement saying he was saddened by the "enormous tragedy" in Guam. He ordered urgent government help for relatives of the victims.
In a KAL building near the Seoul airport, wailing relatives of passengers awaited news of their loved ones.
"My mother, my sister, her husband and their daughter have all been listed among the dead," cried Lim Yong-kyu, 38, who collapsed on the ground, tears streaming from his eyes.
Scores of weeping women held their hands together as they moved around in search of news on their relatives.
Son Seon-nyo, 24, jumped with joy after her sister, a flight attendant, was confirmed as a survivor.

A KAL official said Flight 801 was upgraded from an Airbus to the larger Boeing 747 because of an increase in tourists to Guam during the current summer holiday season. "We often upgrade planes on the route to meet growing demand," he said.

Guam governor Carl Gutierrez described the crash scene as eerie. "I heard screams from every corner of the darkness," he said, adding that he rescued about five people including an 11-year-old Japanese girl but failed to save her mother.
